issues.display_title: Issue #140: Fix the Feedback folder in api-collection: auth variable, feedbackId, and baseUrl
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Feedback API Collection Fixes ( Task #140 / PR #142 )

Summary

Implemented issue #140 in PR #142. The Bruno feedback collection now uses the environment's bearer token, provides reusable feedback IDs, points the DEV environment at the deployed API, and documents the current /v1/auth/me response.

This change affects collection documentation and test configuration only. API behavior, routes, models, and database schema remain unchanged.

Authentication Fix

The Feedback folder previously inherited this nonexistent variable:

token: "{{token}}"

It now uses the collection-wide convention:

token: "{{bearerToken}}"

All five feedback requests inherit this folder authentication:

  • Submit feedback
  • List support feedback
  • Get support feedback
  • Update support feedback
  • Reply to support feedback

Setting bearerToken once in the selected Bruno environment therefore authenticates every feedback request.

Environment Variables

Both environments now define:

- name: feedbackId
  value: <FEEDBACK_ID>

The value is consumed by the feedback detail, update, and reply requests. Testers can paste one created feedback ID into the environment instead of editing three request URLs.

DEV.yml also now defines:

- name: baseUrl
  value: http://192.168.1.226:7070
- name: bearerToken
  value: <YOUR_JWT_TOKEN>

Local - Dev.yml keeps http://127.0.0.1:7070 and its existing bearerToken placeholder.

Current User Example

The successful /v1/auth/me examples now include:

{
  "role": "support",
  "has_password": true
}

The obsolete example content-length header was removed because adding response fields makes the old fixed length incorrect. Endpoint documentation now mentions role and password availability.

Files Changed

  • api-collection/v1/feedback/folder.yml
  • api-collection/environments/DEV.yml
  • api-collection/environments/Local - Dev.yml
  • api-collection/v1/auth/me/Get current user.yml

Usage

  1. Import or reload the Bruno collection.
  2. Select DEV or Local - Dev.
  3. Replace <YOUR_JWT_TOKEN> with a valid token for a user whose global role is support.
  4. Run Submit feedback or use an existing feedback record.
  5. Replace <FEEDBACK_ID> with that feedback ID.
  6. Run all five feedback requests and Get current user.

Expected results:

  • Requests no longer return 401 because of the old missing token variable.
  • Support-only requests authorize when the selected user has role=support.
  • Get current user returns role and has_password.

Verification

Static verification confirmed:

  • No {{token}} reference remains in the collection.
  • Feedback folder auth uses {{bearerToken}}.
  • Both environments define feedbackId.
  • DEV uses http://192.168.1.226:7070 and defines bearerToken.
  • Both successful current-user examples contain role and has_password.
  • git diff --check passes.

The DEV API was reachable on port 7070 and returned 401 without credentials, confirming the endpoint address. A complete six-request manual run still requires a valid support token and feedback record ID.

Follow-up to the feedback endpoint series (#123–#126, #136). Not a code defect — the API behaves correctly; the Bruno collection that documents it does not.

Description

1. The Feedback folder authenticates with a variable that does not exist.

api-collection/v1/feedback/folder.yml:8:

auth:
  type: bearer
  token: "{{token}}"

No environment defines token. environments/Local - Dev.yml and environments/DEV.yml define only baseUrl, bearerToken, and googleIdToken. Counting across the whole collection: {{bearerToken}} appears 31 times, {{token}} appears once — here.

All five feedback requests declare auth: inherit, so every one of them sends an empty bearer and gets 401, even when the tester has pasted a valid token into the environment. The endpoints themselves are fine; this was verified live against the deployed API with a real support token, where all five respond correctly.

Feedback is also the only folder in the collection that declares its own auth: block. Every other folder leaves auth to the individual request, e.g. api-collection/v1/auth/me/Get current user.yml:

  auth:
    type: bearer
    token: "{{bearerToken}}"

Introduced in 63449c8 and inherited by each later feedback PR.

2. {{feedbackId}} is never defined. It is used by Get support feedback.yml, Update support feedback.yml, and Reply to support feedback.yml, but appears in neither environment, so those three requests cannot be run without editing the URL by hand.

3. No environment points at a reachable server. Three different values, none of them the dev API at 192.168.1.226:7070:

File baseUrl
opencollection.yml http://localhost:9999
environments/DEV.yml http://<SERVER_IP>:9999 — literal placeholder, and the port is wrong
environments/Local - Dev.yml http://127.0.0.1:7070

4. The /v1/auth/me example response is stale. It shows name, email, avatar, email_verified only. src/controllers/v1/auth/me.go:33-34 has returned role and has_password since #121. This one matters beyond tidiness: the frontend task GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#583 reads the support role from this endpoint, and a developer checking the collection would conclude the field is not there yet.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The Feedback folder authenticates with {{bearerToken}} — either fix the token name in folder.yml or drop the folder-level block and give each request its own auth, matching the rest of the collection
  • All five feedback requests return something other than 401 when a valid support token is set in the environment
  • feedbackId added to both environment files with a placeholder value
  • DEV.yml baseUrl points at the real dev API, port included
  • The /v1/auth/me example response includes role and has_password
  • Manual check: import the collection, set bearerToken for a role=support user, and run all five feedback requests plus Get current user

Notes

The submit endpoint (POST /v1/feedback) is affected too — it sits in the same folder, so it also inherits the broken auth.

issues.display_title: Issue #141: Stripe webhook signing secret is logged in plaintext on signature failure
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Stripe Webhook Secret Redaction

Summary

Implemented issue #141 in PR #143. Invalid Stripe webhook signatures no longer cause STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET to be written to application logs.

The webhook remains public and continues to authenticate Stripe callbacks through the Stripe-Signature header. Only diagnostic logging changed; event verification and billing behavior remain unchanged.

Security Issue

The previous invalid-signature log rendered the signing secret with %q:

log.Printf("... Secret: %q ...", secret)

Anyone could trigger this path by sending an invalid signature to:

POST /v1/billing/webhook

Users with access to pm2 output, container logs, or log shipping could then read the secret and forge Stripe webhook signatures.

Fix

The log now records only the secret length:

log.Printf(
    "WEBHOOK ERROR - Body Len: %d | Signature Len: %d | Secret Len: %d | Error: %v\n",
    len(body), len(signature), len(secret), err,
)

The length preserves a useful presence/configuration signal without exposing secret material. Webhook validation failures still return 400.

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/billing/webhook.go
  • src/action/v1/billing/webhook_test.go

No route, model, database, environment-file, or migration changes were required.

Regression Test

TestWebhookInvalidSignatureDoesNotLogSigningSecret:

  1. Sets a known STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
  2. Captures the standard logger output.
  3. Sends a webhook request with an invalid signature.
  4. Verifies the response is 400.
  5. Verifies the raw signing secret is absent from logs.
  6. Verifies the log contains only Secret Len: 31 for the test value.
  7. Restores the process-wide logger configuration during cleanup.

Secret Log Audit

Go log call sites were audited against these secret environment names:

  • STRIPE_*
  • USEPLUNK_SECRET_KEY
  • JWT_SECRET
  • MINIO_SECRET_KEY

No other log statement was found printing these secrets.

Verification

Commands used:

go test ./src/action/v1/billing -run TestWebhookInvalidSignatureDoesNotLogSigningSecret -count=1
go test ./src/action/v1/billing -count=1
go build ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

The focused regression test, billing package tests, build, vet, and diff check passed. The repository-wide test suite still had the unrelated existing TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents failure: its test expects /predict/txt, while current production code calls /txt.

Required Operational Action

The old signing secret must be treated as compromised because it may remain in retained logs. Merging the code fix prevents future exposure but does not invalidate previously leaked values.

After deploying PR #143:

  1. Rotate the webhook signing secret in Stripe Dashboard.
  2. Replace STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in every deployed environment.
  3. Restart the API processes so they load the new value.
  4. Send a Stripe test webhook and confirm signature verification succeeds.
  5. Revoke or remove the previous secret after the new configuration is verified.

Do not write either old or new secret into repository files, issue comments, PR comments, or logs.

Pre-existing, unrelated to the feedback series — found while reviewing #139.

Description

src/action/v1/billing/webhook.go:32 writes the Stripe webhook signing secret to stdout in plaintext every time signature verification fails:

log.Printf("WEBHOOK ERROR - Body Len: %d | Signature Len: %d | Secret: %q | Error: %v\n",
    len(body), len(signature), secret, err)

secret is os.Getenv("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET") (line 27), rendered raw with %q. Note the line is otherwise careful — body and signature are logged as lengths precisely so their contents do not leak — so the secret is the one value that was meant to be described and instead gets printed.

POST /v1/billing/webhook is public (src/routes/v1/billing.go:16, no middleware.Auth()), so anyone who can reach the endpoint can trigger the log line at will by posting a body with a bad signature.

Anyone with log access — the pm2 output, the container logs, or any shipper they are forwarded to — can read the signing secret and forge webhook events that the API will accept as genuine Stripe callbacks. Billing state is driven by those events (customer.subscription.created, customer.subscription.updated), so a forged event can change a subscription.

This also conflicts with the documented convention in src/config/database.go:51, where query parameters are suppressed from logs with the comment "Jangan log parameter (seperti email) untuk alasan keamanan".

Acceptance Criteria

  • The signing secret is no longer written to logs — log its length if a presence check is useful, consistent with how body and signature are handled on the same line
  • No other log statement in the repo prints a secret; grep for STRIPE_, USEPLUNK_SECRET_KEY, JWT_SECRET, and MINIO_SECRET_KEY against log. call sites
  • STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET rotated in the Stripe dashboard and in the deployed environment after the fix ships — the current value must be assumed compromised, since it may already sit in retained logs
  • Test: a webhook request with an invalid signature still returns 400 and the emitted log line contains no secret material

Notes

Fixing the code does not undo prior exposure. The rotation is the part that actually closes it, so please treat it as part of the task rather than a follow-up.

issues.display_title: Issue #144: Support feedback list cannot filter by solved/unsolved in one request
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback Multi-Status Filter

Summary

Implemented issue #144. GET /v1/support/feedback now accepts multiple comma-separated status values, allowing the support dashboard to request complete solved or unsolved result sets before pagination.

Existing single-status requests remain compatible.

API Usage

Solved feedback:

GET /v1/support/feedback?status=resolved,closed

Unsolved feedback:

GET /v1/support/feedback?status=new,reviewing,replied

Single-status filtering still works:

GET /v1/support/feedback?status=reviewing

The parameter composes with existing search, category, area, project, sorting, and pagination parameters.

Validation

The endpoint:

  1. Splits status on commas.
  2. Trims whitespace around every value.
  3. Validates every value against the existing status set:
    • new
    • reviewing
    • replied
    • resolved
    • closed
  4. Returns 400 when any value is empty or invalid.

Examples returning 400:

status=invalid
status=resolved,invalid
status=resolved,,closed

Query Behavior

Validated status values are applied through a parameterized GORM query:

query.Where("status IN ?", statuses)

The filtered query is used for both:

  • total count calculation
  • Paginated feedback retrieval

This ensures the pager and dashboard totals represent the complete solved or unsolved dataset instead of only the current page.

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/feedback/read.go
  • src/action/v1/feedback/read_test.go
  • api-collection/v1/feedback/List support feedback.yml

No route, model, database, or migration changes were required.

Tests

Coverage includes:

  • Exact solved membership: resolved and closed.
  • Exact unsolved membership: new, reviewing, and replied.
  • Correct total for both grouped filters.
  • Existing single-status compatibility.
  • Whitespace trimming around CSV values.
  • Invalid single values.
  • Mixed valid and invalid values.
  • Empty values inside a comma-separated list.

API Collection

The Bruno list request documents the comma-separated status format and includes the unsolved example:

status=new,reviewing,replied

Its documentation also identifies:

  • Solved: resolved,closed
  • Unsolved: new,reviewing,replied

Verification

Commands used:

go test ./src/action/v1/feedback -count=1
go build ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

The feedback tests, build, vet, and diff check passed. The repository-wide suite still has the unrelated existing TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents failure: its test expects /predict/txt, while current production code calls /txt.

Raised while implementing the frontend list alignment (GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#584). Follow-up to #124 and #136.

Description

The support dashboard's primary control is a Solved / Unsolved / All filter. It cannot be expressed as a request today, so it runs client-side over whatever page the frontend happens to be holding — which, since pagination shipped in #136, means it narrows the current page only. Ask for "unsolved" on a table of 500 and you get the unsolved rows out of the 20 in hand, not the unsolved rows overall.

The gap is that "solved" is two statuses, not one:

// frontend: src/app/support/SupportDashboardClient.tsx
function isSolved(status) { return status === "resolved" || status === "closed" }

while GET /v1/support/feedback takes a single value:

// src/action/v1/feedback/read.go
query = query.Where("status = ?", value)

so ?status=resolved misses closed, and there is no way to ask for "either". The same is true in reverse for unsolved, which is new, reviewing, and replied together.

The counts are affected as well: the dashboard header shows a solved/unsolved split that is page-scoped for the same reason. The frontend currently labels that pair "on this page" so the numbers do not claim to be global, but that is a description of the limitation, not a fix.

Options

Either would work; the first is smaller and composes with the existing validation.

  1. Let status accept a comma-separated list — ?status=resolved,closed — validating each value against validStatuses and using IN (?). Existing single-value callers keep working unchanged.
  2. Add a dedicated ?solved=true|false parameter that maps to the two groupings server-side.

Whichever is chosen, total must reflect the same filter so the frontend pager stays correct.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The list endpoint can return exactly the solved set (resolved + closed) or the unsolved set (new + reviewing + replied) in one request
  • Invalid values still produce 400, consistent with the current status validation
  • total respects the new filter, so pagination stays correct
  • Existing single-value ?status= requests keep working
  • Tests: solved set, unsolved set, invalid value → 400, and total correct under the new filter
  • api-collection/v1/feedback/List support feedback.yml documents the parameter

Frontend counterpart

Once this ships, the solved filter moves into the request and the header counts can be sourced from the server instead of the page. Tracked against gothru-3d-floormap#584.
